articles.title: China points to problems with Belgium-Chile joint candidature to host UN marine biodiversity secretariat
articles.titleCn: 中国指出比利时-智利联合申办联合国海洋生物多样性秘书处所在地的问题
articles.summary: China on Thursday called on the international community to find a home for the Secretariat of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) best positioned for its efficient operation, pointing out problems with the joint candidature by Belgium and Chile.

paragraphs.en: Noting the BBNJ Secretariat is tasked with contributing to global ocean governance, and the selection of its seat should be a fair and friendly process in keeping with the rules, Mao said the Belgium-Chile proposal, however, {{15}} the bidding process and attempts to divide Parties into camps. "It not only {{16}} the principle of fair, friendly and healthy competition, but also negates the essence of {{18}}," she said. Sixth, it contravenes the original commitment. Chile first made the bid citing its significance for the Global South. Yet according to the new proposal, Chile will no longer assume the substantive functions of the secretariat.
paragraphs.cn: 毛宁指出，BBNJ秘书处的任务是促进全球海洋治理，其所在地的选择应是一个符合规则的公平友好过程，但比利时-智利提案却将申办过程政治化，并试图将缔约方划分为不同阵营。她说：“这不仅损害了公平、友好和良性竞争的原则，也否定了多边主义的本质。”第六，它违反了最初的承诺。智利最初申办时称其对全球南方具有重要意义。然而根据新提案，智利将不再承担秘书处的实质性职能。

paragraphs.en: Belgium, for its part, only seeks to host the CHM and thereby has in effect {{17}} its bid for the secretariat seat, Mao said. Stressing that the adoption and entry into force of the BBNJ Agreement is a victory of multilateralism, Mao said its implementation likewise needs to serve and advance the common well-being of all humanity. "We call on the international community to find a home for the secretariat best positioned for its efficient operation and the effective implementation of the agreement," Mao said, adding that China firmly supports multilateralism and the cause of the UN, and is committed to promoting and improving global ocean governance. She said that as one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China has the will, capability and confidence to provide strong support and backing for the operation of the secretariat. "China is full ready.

articles.fullText:
China on Thursday called on the international community to find a home for the Secretariat of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) best positioned for its efficient operation, pointing out problems with the joint candidature by Belgium and Chile.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing after Belgium and Chile on Nov. 6 announced the decision to join their candidatures for the seat of the secretariat. This joint candidature provides for the secretariat being based in the city of Valparaíso, Chile, the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM) will be installed in and operating from Brussels, and Brussels will host the meetings of the subsidiary bodies.
Mao said that earlier this year, China nominated Xiamen to bid for the seat of the Secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement, noting that the candidature has quickly received the support of the majority of the Parties to the Agreement.
"By seeking an unauthorized backroom deal on issues that should be determined by the Conference of the Parties (COP), the joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects," the spokesperson said.
First, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement. According to the agreement, the seat of the secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the CHM, including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by COP, and the CHM shall be managed by the secretariat, she said.
"Belgium and Chile traded under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties to the Agreement. This is a violation of the stipulations of the agreement and an act of disrespect to the authority of COP," Mao said.
Second, it contravenes procedural justice, Mao said, adding that the choice of the secretariat seat and the development of the CHM are two items of different nature scheduled to be collectively determined by COP through separate decisions.
The Belgium-Chile proposal bundles the two together in an attempt to force it as a package upon other Parties, which is against applicable procedural rules and a hijack of the Parties' will, she said.
Third, it contravenes established international practice. Stressing that the management of the CHM is a key mandate of the secretariat, Mao said in the practice established by other international treaties like the Convention on Biological Diversity, the secretariats and CHMs are located in the same place.
"The Belgium-Chile proposal, which locates the Secretariat and the CHM separately across the ocean, will without a doubt raise the operation cost, lower management efficiency, and increase the financial burden on the Parties to the Agreement," Mao said.
Fourth, it contravenes equitable geographical distribution. The vast majority of major global institutions are based in Europe, with none located in Asia. Developing countries have been calling on global institutions to redress this long-existing injustice and bring about greater fairness and equity, the spokesperson said.
She said Brussels is already home to the headquarters of NATO and the EU. "If this non-coastal city were to host the CHM of an ocean-related treaty as well, it would further widen the digital divide to the detriment of the shared interests of the Global South."
Fifth, it contravenes fair competition. Noting the BBNJ Secretariat is tasked with contributing to global ocean governance, and the selection of its seat should be a fair and friendly process in keeping with the rules, Mao said the Belgium-Chile proposal, however, politicizes the bidding process and attempts to divide Parties into camps.
"It not only undermines the principle of fair, friendly and healthy competition, but also negates the essence of multilateralism," she said.
Sixth, it contravenes the original commitment. Chile first made the bid citing its significance for the Global South. Yet according to the new proposal, Chile will no longer assume the substantive functions of the secretariat. Belgium, for its part, only seeks to host the CHM and thereby has in effect relinquished its bid for the secretariat seat, Mao said.
Stressing that the adoption and entry into force of the BBNJ Agreement is a victory of multilateralism, Mao said its implementation likewise needs to serve and advance the common well-being of all humanity.
"We call on the international community to find a home for the secretariat best positioned for its efficient operation and the effective implementation of the agreement," Mao said, adding that China firmly supports multilateralism and the cause of the UN, and is committed to promoting and improving global ocean governance.
She said that as one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China has the will, capability and confidence to provide strong support and backing for the operation of the secretariat.
"China is full ready. We look forward to working with all Parties to the Agreement to keep the selection of the secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, and uphold the overall and fundamental interests of the international community, especially those of developing countries," Mao said.

articles.title: 2026 World Ocean Week spotlights China's ocean governance role
articles.titleCn: 2026世界海洋周聚焦中国在全球海洋治理中的角色
articles.summary: 2026 World Ocean Week spotlights China's ocean governance role
articles.summaryCn: 2026世界海洋周在厦门开幕，发布BBNJ协定双语报告等五项成果，展示中国在海洋生态保护、深海科研与国际合作方面的贡献。

paragraphs.en: The 2026 World Ocean Week opened on November 5 in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province, {{0}} five outcomes, including a publication on seamounts and a {{1}} ecological and environmental data product. The week also features 33 activities, including seminars on marine science and ecology and industry and business matchmaking events, to advance global ocean {{2}} and the high-quality development of the blue economy. A view of Xiamen in Fujian Province, southeast China. A bilingual report on the status, role and {{3}} of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement), and China's role in it, was released on the same day. Compiled by the China Institute for Marine Development Strategy under the Ministry of Natural Resources, the report outlines the {{6}} of the agreement's entry into force and China's contributions to its negotiation and {{7}}.
paragraphs.cn: 2026世界海洋周于11月5日在中国东南部福建省厦门市开幕，发布了五项成果，包括一份关于海山的出版物和一项专门的生态环境数据产品。本周还举办33项活动，包括海洋科学与生态研讨会以及产业与商业对接活动，以推进全球海洋治理和蓝色经济的高质量发展。中国东南部福建省厦门市一景。同日发布了一份中英双语报告，介绍《联合国海洋法公约》下关于国家管辖范围以外区域海洋生物多样性的养护和可持续利用协定（BBNJ协定）的现状、作用与前景，以及中国在其中的角色。该报告由自然资源部下属的中国海洋发展战略研究所编制，概述了该协定生效的意义以及中国对其谈判和实施所作的贡献。

paragraphs.en: The BBNJ Agreement took effect on January 17, 2026, becoming the third implementing agreement to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and filling a legal gap in the {{8}} and governance of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national {{4}}. China participated in nearly 20 years of negotiations and put forward proposals on the agreement's four key areas. Its contributions included promoting a benefit-sharing mechanism for marine genetic resources, advancing area-based management tools, improving {{9}} in environmental impact assessments and helping developing countries build capacity to implement the agreement. China has {{10}} marine ecological conservation redlines covering about 150,000 square kilometers, established 353 marine protected areas and carried out 194 marine ecological conservation projects. It is also one of the few countries worldwide to have recorded a net increase in mangrove area.
paragraphs.cn: BBNJ协定于2026年1月17日生效，成为《联合国海洋法公约》的第三份执行协定，填补了国家管辖范围以外区域海洋生物多样性养护与治理方面的法律空白。中国参与了近20年的谈判，并就协定的四个关键领域提出了建议。其贡献包括推动海洋遗传资源惠益分享机制、推进划区管理工具、提高环境影响评估的透明度，以及帮助发展中国家建设执行该协定的能力。中国划定了覆盖约15万平方公里的海洋生态保护红线，建立了353个海洋保护地，并实施了194个海洋生态保护项目。中国还是全球少数几个红树林面积实现净增加的国家之一。

paragraphs.en: China has made manned deep-sea {{11}} Jiaolong and Fendouzhe, as well as research vessels such as Deep Sea No. 1, available for international scientific {{12}}. It preserves nearly 60,000 marine microbial resources and provides international users with access to samples and data. Under the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development, China has led 10 major international science programs, including one on the digital discovery of typical deep-sea habitats. China has improved its legal framework for environmental impact assessments of activities in the international seabed area, while contractors engaged in mineral exploration there have actively fulfilled their assessment {{13}}.

The 2026 World Ocean Week opened on November 5 in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province, unveiling five outcomes, including a publication on seamounts and a dedicated ecological and environmental data product.
The week also features 33 activities, including seminars on marine science and ecology and industry and business matchmaking events, to advance global ocean governance and the high-quality development of the blue economy.
A view of Xiamen in Fujian Province, southeast China. 
A bilingual report on the status, role and prospects of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement), and China's role in it, was released on the same day.
Compiled by the China Institute for Marine Development Strategy under the Ministry of Natural Resources, the report outlines the significance of the agreement's entry into force and China's contributions to its negotiation and implementation.
The BBNJ Agreement took effect on January 17, 2026, becoming the third implementing agreement to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and filling a legal gap in the conservation and governance of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
China participated in nearly 20 years of negotiations and put forward proposals on the agreement's four key areas. Its contributions included promoting a benefit-sharing mechanism for marine genetic resources, advancing area-based management tools, improving transparency in environmental impact assessments and helping developing countries build capacity to implement the agreement.
China has designated marine ecological conservation redlines covering about 150,000 square kilometers, established 353 marine protected areas and carried out 194 marine ecological conservation projects. It is also one of the few countries worldwide to have recorded a net increase in mangrove area.
China has made manned deep-sea submersibles Jiaolong and Fendouzhe, as well as research vessels such as Deep Sea No. 1, available for international scientific expeditions. It preserves nearly 60,000 marine microbial resources and provides international users with access to samples and data.
Under the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development, China has led 10 major international science programs, including one on the digital discovery of typical deep-sea habitats.
China has improved its legal framework for environmental impact assessments of activities in the international seabed area, while contractors engaged in mineral exploration there have actively fulfilled their assessment obligations.
Its experience, environmental data, expertise, and trained personnel can help developing countries assess deep-sea activities and promote a greener, low-carbon approach to ocean activities.
China has signed marine cooperation agreements with more than 50 countries and international organizations, established over 40 marine research centers and joint laboratories, and invested about 200 million yuan (about $30 million) in more than 100 small-scale marine cooperation projects. It has also held more than 300 training courses in marine science, technology and management, benefiting over 6,000 young researchers and officials from developing countries.
China was among the first countries to sign and become a party to the BBNJ Agreement. It has applied to host the agreement's secretariat in Xiamen and says it is willing and able to provide sustained support for the agreement's full and effective implementation.

(ECNS) -- Climate change poses the biggest threat to the vision of ecological civilization, and no country can tackle the global challenge alone, said Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, on Thursday.
Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, made the remarks at the China-Türkiye Dialogue on Ecological Civilization and Green Transition held in Istanbul during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), which kicked off on Monday in the Turkish coastal city of Antalya.
The dialogue was hosted by China News Service and the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, with China News Network and the Policy Research Center for Environment and Economy of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (PRCEE) as co-organizers. It's also the second multilateral event of China News Service’s flagship program "News Lounge" held in Türkiye.
Coşar said ecological civilization is, in its broadest sense, a philosophical and political concept aimed at rebuilding the relationship between humanity and nature on the basis of balance and sustainability, in response to the global climate crisis and ecological degradation.
He noted that discussions on ecological civilization, known in Chinese as "shengtai wenming," began in China in the 1980s. In 2018, the concept was incorporated into China's Constitution as a national goal.
Coşar outlined three key features of ecological civilization. First, it rejects a development model that treats humanity as the master of nature and seeks to protect life and biodiversity. Second, it places natural ecological assets and sustainability at the center of economic structures, moving beyond growth models focused primarily on GDP. Third, it represents political and social transformation that integrates socialism with ecological principles, as reflected in China's national strategy.
Addressing the challenges posed by climate change, Coşar said humanity's continued pursuit of a more comfortable lifestyle, along with industrial production, technological development, and warfare, has placed growing pressure on the environment and contributed to greenhouse gas emissions. He noted that while industrialization and technological progress have driven social development, they have also brought significant ecological challenges that should not be overlooked.
The impact of warfare is particularly concerning. Beyond the direct destruction of natural environments and ecosystems, war-related activities also generate substantial emissions, with environmental consequences that may persist for a long time and affect future generations. Climate change, he stressed, is therefore not only a challenge facing today's societies but also a global issue with long-term implications.
Coşar stressed that climate change is a global phenomenon that cannot be addressed by any country acting alone. He also expressed concern that some of the countries contributing most to global pollution are taking the fewest measures to combat climate change.
Coşar concluded by emphasizing that climate change is a long-term and complex global challenge with far-reaching consequences. Given the evolving climate situation, no country can achieve its vision of ecological civilization on its own, making stronger international cooperation essential to advancing ecological civilization worldwide.

(ECNS) -- China's approach to ecological civilization offers an important model for the global energy transition and green energy cooperation projects developed under the Belt and Road Initiative present major opportunities for countries such as Türkiye, Nadir Temeloğlu, editor-in-chief of Türkiye's Ulusal Kanal, spoke at the China-Türkiye Dialogue on Ecological Civilization and Green Transformation in Istanbul on Thursday local time.
The dialogue was held during the ongoing 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).
The event was co-hosted by China News Service and the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, co-organized by China News Network and the Policy Research Center for Environment and Economy of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment.
It also marks the second time China News Service has brought its "News Lounge" interviews to Türkiye.
Representatives from government departments, research institutions, enterprises, and media from both China and Türkiye attended the event.
In a speech at the dialogue, Temeloğlu addressed topics including climate justice, energy transition and Türkiye-China green energy cooperation.
He said the climate crisis is not merely an environmental problem, but also a question of injustice. In his view, current climate policies risk perpetuating and even reproducing these inequalities. The solution, he said, lies in establishing a worldview that prioritizes the shared interests of all humanity.
Temeloğlu believed that overcoming this crisis needs a vision of an Ecological Civilization built upon egalitarian, cooperative and solidarity based values that prioritize harmony between humanity and nature.
He also stressed that new energy must be affordable, readily accessible, renewable and environmentally benign. To this end, renewable energy sources and green hydrogen should come to the fore.
Temeloğlu particularly noted that China's approach to ecological civilization offers an important reference to global countries. He said that China treats environmental pollution brought on by rapid economic growth as an existential challenge and has placed ecological transformation at the heart of its national security strategy.
He also said that China's efforts to advance ecological civilization in areas such as clean energy development, green agriculture and sustainable urbanization constitute an exemplary model.
Temeloğlu also discussed bilateral green energy cooperation between Türkiye and China under the Belt and Road Initiative.
He said such projects have brought major opportunities to Türkiye and other countries.
Green energy cooperation projects developed under the initiative also present major opportunities for countries such as Türkiye.
Green energy cooperation between countries such as China and Türkiye will accelerate their development and help build a more just international order, he said.
He concluded that the green transition cannot be achieved through isolated national actions alone and that genuine solutions can come only from an approach centered on public interest, sharing, solidarity and equality among nations.

articles.fullText:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Tuesday called for a people-centered approach to Internet development and stronger international cooperation to jointly build a community with a shared future in cyberspace.
Speaking at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in east China's Zhejiang Province, Li said the Internet is undergoing an intelligent transformation and a systemic leap as it converges at an accelerating pace with with technologies such as AI, cloud computing and blockchain.
He said the Internet is not merely infrastructure, but also shaping new ways of life, driving industrial transformation and fostering intelligent generation.
Li stressed that AI and the Internet should extend human capabilities and serve as means of liberation, not replace people. Human agency must remain paramount and the ultimate purpose must be to promote people's all-round development, he said.
He also highlighted the need to tackle the ethical implications of algorithms and models, the security risks arising from digital-physical integration, and the digital and AI divide, noting that over two billion people worldwide remain offline.
To address these challenges, Li put forward four proposals:
1. Open innovation. Bolster scientific and technological innovation, encourage open source, strengthen collaborative research, and support the large-scale application of new tech and products. Li said China will continue to promote technology transfer and knowledge sharing to build an open, inclusive and dynamic global ecosystem for digital innovation.
2. Digital security. Ensure credibility and controllability to strengthen digital security safeguards. Li urged countries to promote common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and step up practical cooperation. China will respect the legitimate cybersecurity concerns of all countries, he said, while opposing the overstretching of the concept of national security and the erection of "digital iron curtains."
3. Inclusive development. Pursue universally beneficial and balanced development to share digital dividends. Li said China will actively implement the Global Development Initiative and support Global South countries in building digital infrastructure, cultivating talent and enhancing capacity.
4. Multilateral governance. Advance open dialogue to improve the multilateral governance system. Li called for strengthening coordination and cooperation rather than deliberately escalating friction, practicing true multilateralism, maximizing common interests and promoting more just and equitable global Internet governance. China will actively build dialogue platforms based on the principle of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, and contribute more Chinese wisdom to improving cyberspace governance, he said.
Li noted that in an increasingly interconnected world, no country can prosper alone. China will work with the international community to ensure that digital and intelligent technologies better serve global development and the well-being of all humanity, he said.

2. 数字安全。确保可信可控，加强数字安全保障。李强敦促各国推动共同、综合、合作、可持续的安全，加强务实合作。他说，中国将尊重各国的正当网络安全关切，同时反对过度延伸国家安全概念和竖起“数字铁幕”。
